question: Which of the following is satisfied by all numbers \(x\) of the form \[ x=\frac{a_1}{3}+\frac{a_2}{3^2}+\cdots+\frac{a_{25}}{3^{25}}, \] where \(a_1\) is \(0\) or \(2,\) \(a_2\) is \(0\) or \(2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(a_{25}\) is \(0\) or \(2?\)
solution:
The first term is either \(0\) or \(2/3\). To locate \(x\), we can therefore bound how much all the remaining terms contribute. Write
\[
x=\frac{a_1}{3}+R,
\qquad R=\frac{a_2}{3^2}+\cdots+\frac{a_{25}}{3^{25}}.
\]
Every term of \(R\) is nonnegative, and replacing every remaining coefficient by \(2\) gives its largest possible value. The resulting sum has \(24\) terms, first term \(2/9\), and common ratio \(1/3\). By the finite geometric sum formula,
\[
0\le R\le\frac29\cdot\frac{1-(1/3)^{24}}{1-1/3}
=\frac13-\frac1{3^{25}}<\frac13.
\]
If \(a_1=0\), this gives \(0\le x<1/3\). If \(a_1=2\), it gives
\[
\frac23\le x\le 1-\frac1{3^{25}}<1.
\]
These two cases cover every allowed choice, so D always holds. To eliminate the other choices, taking all coefficients to be zero gives \(x=0\), which rules out B, C, and E. Taking \(a_1=2\) and all other coefficients zero gives \(x=2/3\), which rules out A. Thus the answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
